title: RRC Framework Coverage records which risk model prices an Instance, not whether the Instance is compliant
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.3 supplies the definition that Instance Configuration Documents elsewhere assume: "The `RRC Framework Full Implementation Coverage` status defines whether the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model … or a pending risk model … If the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model the status is `Covered`. If the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a pending risk model the status is `Pending`."

This reframes the field entirely. Read without the definition, a `Pending` Instance looks like an uncovered exposure — capital deployed before risk work was finished. Read with it, `Pending` means the Instance *is* assigned Required Risk Capital, just computed under a pending rather than fully implemented model. Both branches exist in the Risk Capital framework (A.3.2.1.1.4.3.1 and A.3.2.1.1.4.3.2); neither is an absence.

The field is therefore a **model-provenance flag**, and its purpose is to make the basis of a capital number auditable rather than to gate deployment. Someone assessing the ecosystem's aggregate risk capital can separate exposures priced by a mature model from those priced by a provisional one, and weight their confidence accordingly.

Obex's Maple USDC Instance carries `Covered` (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.1) — the fully implemented case. The design implication is that pending models are expected to exist in production indefinitely, since new venues will always outpace model development; what the framework insists on is that the distinction never be invisible.
description: `Covered` means the Instance Financial RRC is calculated from a fully implemented risk model and `Pending` means it uses a pending one
